title: Frame Assembly
summary: A light square wooden frame with a square hole near each corner stands upright on the ground in front of a wall, and four metal pegs stick straight out of the wall's front face in a square pattern that matches the holes. Mount the frame on the pegs: success needs the frame's centre within 5 cm of the centre of the four-peg pattern in the wall's plane (sideways and vertically together) and within 10 cm of it along the wall's normal.
scene: The ground is the world's z = 0 plane. In front of the robot stands an immovable (kinematic) wall: a slab 0.1 m thick, 2.0 m wide and 2.0 m tall with a concrete-block surface, its front face turned toward the robot. The wall is upright (no tilt in this task); its distance and sideways offset vary between instances. Four fixed (kinematic) iron pegs, cylinders 4 cm in diameter and 15 cm long, stick straight out of the wall's front face toward the robot at the corners of a 0.4 m square centred on the wall's centre, and move with the wall. A short distance in front of the wall, a frame of oak-textured square bars stands upright on its bottom edge on the ground, facing the robot: 0.52 m square and 2 cm thick, bars 2 cm wide, and inside each corner a square ring that leaves an 8 cm square hole; the four hole centres also form a 0.4 m square. A small block hangs from the middle of the top bar on the inside (visual only, it has no collision). The frame is a free rigid body of 10 g; its place on the ground varies by several centimetres between instances. Nothing moves by itself. The robot starts hovering level and motionless, facing the wall, with its arm at its zero joint configuration (end effector a little ahead of and above the airframe) and the gripper closed.
scene_privileged: One environment; its origin is the world origin. Robot at every reset: base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) m with orientation (1, 0, 0, 0) wxyz (body +x is the world +x direction), zero velocity; arm_link1_pitch_joint = arm_link2_pitch_joint = arm_link3_pitch_joint = arm_link4_roll_joint = 0 rad; arm_lfinger_joint = arm_rfinger_joint = 0.001 m (their lower limit: gripper closed, gripper_width 0.002 m). By the robot's URDF kinematics this puts ee_link at about (0.227, 0, 1.124) m with identity orientation and the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + 0.18 m along the ee_link x axis) at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m; the end-effector command is initialised to the current ee_link pose. Wall: kinematic cuboid 0.1 (x) x 2.0 (y) x 2.0 (z) m, nominal centre (2.0, 0.0, 1.0) m and orientation identity (front face the plane x = centre_x - 0.05, normal -x, toward the robot); friction 1.0 static / 1.0 dynamic, restitution 0; visual material NVIDIA Concrete_Block.mdl. At each reset AM-Bench's randomize_wall_and_pegs sets the centre to (2.0 + dx, 0.0 + dy, 1.0) with dx ~ U(-0.1, 0.1) m and dy ~ U(-0.2, 0.2) m independently (no rotation) and places the four pegs at wall_centre + R_wall (-0.125, +-0.2, +-0.2) m with the wall's orientation. Pegs: peg.usd, kinematic, gravity disabled, a cylinder along the world x axis, radius 0.02 m, length 0.15 m, so each spans x from wall_centre_x - 0.2 to the wall face at wall_centre_x - 0.05; physics material static friction 2.0, dynamic 1.5; visual material vMaterials Iron.mdl, referenced by URL from NVIDIA's content server. Peg centre (mean of the four peg roots; AM-Bench's peg_center_pos observation) = (wall_centre_x - 0.125, wall_centre_y, 1.0). Frame: rigid body frame.usd, dynamic, gravity on, spawned with scale (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) (thickness 0.025 / 0.05, width and height 0.5 / 1.0), mass 0.01 kg (mass_props; the USD authors 0.0001 kg), no physics material bound, visual material Oak.mdl referenced by URL from NVIDIA's content server. In its body frame (origin at the frame's centre, x the thickness axis), after scaling: 20 box colliders, outer bars forming a 0.52 x 0.52 m (y x z) square 0.02 m thick in x and 0.02 m wide, and four corner rings centred at (0, +-0.2, +-0.2) m, 0.12 m outside, with a 0.08 x 0.08 m opening; plus a visual-only 0.02 x 0.02 x 0.06 m block at the top bar's middle, z 0.20..0.26. At each reset (mdp.reset_root_state_uniform) the frame's root is set to (1.7 + fx, 0.0 + fy, 0.25) m with fx ~ U(-0.08, 0.08) m, fy ~ U(-0.12, 0.12) m, identity orientation, zero velocity (AM-Bench's frame_pos observation is this root): upright in the world y-z plane, standing on its bottom bar; as its half height is 0.26 m, that bar starts 1 cm below the ground surface. Scene default physics material: friction 1.0 / 1.0, restitution 0.
success: Success at a control step when, with p the frame's root position (its centre) and c the peg centre (mean of the four peg root positions, = wall centre + R_wall (-0.125, 0, 0)), |p_x - c_x| < 0.1 m and sqrt((p_y - c_y)^2 + (p_z - c_z)^2) < 0.05 m (world axes, strict inequalities; the wall is never rotated, so x is its normal). The pegs run from c_x - 0.075 to c_x + 0.075 m (the wall face). Nothing else is tested: no orientation, velocity, contact or release condition (the frame may still be held). AM-Bench also reports frame_lifted (frame z > its z at reset + 0.05 m) and frame_placed_on_pegs (the success itself); they are informational only. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 30 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 3600 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 3599th step.
difficulty_note: The 0.52 m frame has to be raised from the ground to the pegs and its four 8 cm holes brought over four 4 cm pegs at once, from a hovering base, with the wall's (and so the pegs') position changing per instance.
standard_notes: The poses of the frame, the wall and the pegs are not given: the frame on the ground and the four pegs on the concrete wall have to be located with the forward-looking onboard cameras and related to the robot through proprioception (base and end-effector poses), and whether the frame is centred on the pegs can only be judged visually. Success is not reported during the episode.
